# gitmoap_repository_catalog_resolve (Data Source)

Resolve repository paths to the services that own them. Send each path as a repeated `path` parameter, up to 200 in one call: one request per changed file set rather than one per file. Each answer names the service that owns the path, where the most specific binding wins, and lists any other services whose bindings also match, in resolution order. Anyone who can read the repository's catalog may call it.

The token needs `catalog:read`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "gitmoap_repository_by_path" "api" {
  full_path = "acme/platform/api"
}

data "gitmoap_repository_catalog_resolve" "api" {
  path    = ["services/payments/handler.go"]
  repo_id = data.gitmoap_repository_by_path.api.repository_id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `path` (List of String) A repository-relative path. Repeatable, up to 200 per call — one request per changed file set, not one per file
- `repo_id` (String) The repository the paths belong to

### Read-Only

- `resolved` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--resolved))

<a id="nestedatt--resolved"></a>
### Nested Schema for `resolved`

Read-Only:

- `overlapping` (Attributes List) The other services that also claim the path, in resolution order. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--resolved--overlapping))
- `path` (String)
- `service` (Attributes) The short form of a service that listings, search results and path lookups show. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--resolved--service))

<a id="nestedatt--resolved--overlapping"></a>
### Nested Schema for `resolved.overlapping`

Read-Only:

- `display_name` (String)
- `external` (Boolean)
- `group_id` (String)
- `kind` (String) What sort of thing a service is. The kind decides which scorecard checks apply: a `library` has
no deployments, so a deployment check is not applicable to it rather than failing. For your own
classifications, use annotations.
- `lifecycle` (String) Where a service is in its life.
- `orphaned_at` (String)
- `owner` (Attributes) Who owns a service: a group, a team, or a person or service account. A service may also have no
owner, which the `has_owner` scorecard check surfaces.

`kind` says which applies: `group`, with `full_path`, `group_id`; `principal`, with `actor`, `principal_id`; `team`, with `organization`, `slug`, `team_id`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--resolved--overlapping--owner))
- `service_id` (String)
- `slug` (String)
- `source` (String) How the catalog entry came to exist. Set by the platform, never accepted from a request. Any
source other than `inferred` means a person has vouched for the entry.

<a id="nestedatt--resolved--overlapping--owner"></a>
### Nested Schema for `resolved.overlapping.owner`

Read-Only:

- `actor` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--resolved--overlapping--owner--actor))
- `full_path` (String)
- `group_id` (String)
- `kind` (String)
- `organization` (String) The full path of the organization's top-level group, such as `acme`.
- `principal_id` (String)
- `slug` (String) The team's slug, such as `backend`.
- `team_id` (String)

<a id="nestedatt--resolved--overlapping--owner--actor"></a>
### Nested Schema for `resolved.overlapping.owner.actor`

Read-Only:

- `avatar_url` (String) The principal's picture, when one is known. Absent otherwise: a client derives the
deterministic avatar URL itself.
- `email` (String) The principal's address. An agent's is a generated no-reply address — the author of its
commits. `unknown` on a deleted actor and empty on a redacted one.
- `id` (String) The principal's id: a user id, a service account id or an agent id, as `kind` says. Empty on
a redacted actor.
- `kind` (String) A person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — which of the three a principal is,
and so which page it links to: a person's profile, a service account's page or an agent's page.
- `username` (String) The name to show: a person's or service account's username, or an agent's handle (which
always ends in `-ai`). `deleted-user` when the actor no longer resolves, `redacted` when the
caller may not see who it was. A closed account whose work stays is `closed-` and twelve hex
digits, a shape no open account may take, with an address under `.invalid`.
